blocks.text: Stacks are very useful in managing function calls in programming. Let's break it down with a simple example: Imagine you are making a series of phone calls. Each time you call someone, you write their name on a notepad. When you finish talking, you cross off their name.

items: Making a Call: When you make a call, you write down the name on top of the notepad. This is like pushing information onto the stack.
Ending a Call: After you finish talking, you cross off the name. This is like popping information off the stack.

blocks.text: In programming, when a function is called, its details (like what it needs to do and where to return after it's done) are written on the stack. This helps the computer remember what to do next. When the function finishes, it removes (or pops) its details from the stack, just like crossing off the name.
